items.text:
Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.
While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human?Central to the problem is a person's capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications.
Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them — on habit and practice. We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.
In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. These are areas where _algorithmic_ (算法的) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.
Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.
At the same time, though, this selection is optimizing for what people are likely to prefer based on what they've preferred in the past. We think there is some risk that people's options will be constrained by their past in a new and unanticipated way.
As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. The predictions are going to get better and better, and they will ultimately make common experiences more efficient and pleasant.
Algorithms could soon — if they don't already-have a better idea about which show you'd like to watch next and which job candidate you should hire than you do. One day, humans may even find a way for machines to make these decisions without some of the biases that humans typically display.
But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us.

q5.stem: What do we learn about the deeper implications of AI?
options: It is causing catastrophic levels of unemployment.
It is doing physical harm to human operators.
It is altering moral judgments.
It is reshaping humanity.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.」
排除：A：原文仅提引发失业焦虑，非说正在造成，偷换。；B：未提对操作者身体伤害，无中生有。；C：改变的是判断能力，非道德判断，偷换。
q5.stemCn: 关于人工智能的深层含义，我们了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它正在造成灾难性的失业水平。
它正在对人类操作者造成身体伤害。
它正在改变道德判断。
它正在重塑人性。

q5.stem: What is the consequence of algorithmic prescription replacing human judgment?
options: People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments.
People are prevented from participating in making major decisions in the workplace.
Managers no longer have the chance to decide which loan to approve.
Managers do not need to take the trouble to determine who to hire or fire.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「These are areas where _algorithmic_ (算法的) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.」
排除：B：无中生有；原文未称人被阻止参与职场重大决策。C：范围过窄；原文非只说经理失去审批贷款机会。D：曲解原文；未说经理无需费力决定雇佣或解雇。
q5.stemCn: 算法规定取代人类判断的后果是什么？
optionsCn: 人们失去了培养做出实际判断能力的机会。
人们被阻止参与在工作场所做出重大决定。
经理们不再有机会决定批准哪一笔贷款。
经理们不需要费心去确定雇佣或解雇谁。

q5.stem: What may result from increasing application of recommendation engines in our consumption of culture?
options: Consumers will have much limited choice.
Consumers will actually enjoy better luck.
It will be easier to decide on what to enjoy.
Humans will develop tastes similar to machines'.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck.」
排除：B：与原文相反，会minimize luck；C：无依据，未说决定更容易；D：曲解，机器代替人类品味
q5.stemCn: 在我们文化消费中推荐引擎应用的增加可能会导致什么结果？
optionsCn: 消费者将会有非常有限的选择。
消费者实际上会享受到更好的运气。
决定享受什么会更容易。
人类将培养出与机器相似的品味。

q5.stem: What is likely to happen to larger parts of our daily life as machine learning algorithms improve?
options: They will turn out to be more pleasant.
They will repeat our past experience.
They can be completely anticipated.
They may become better and better.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable.」
排除：A：偷换概念，原文说体验更愉悦，非日常变愉悦。；B：无中生有，原文是受过去偏好约束，非重复经历。；D：张冠李戴，越来越好是预测，非日常。
q5.stemCn: 随着机器学习算法的改进，我们日常生活中的大部分可能会发生什么？
optionsCn: 它们最终会变得更令人愉快。
它们会重复我们过去的经历。
它们可以被完全预测。
它们可能会变得越来越好。

q5.stem: Why does the author say the creatures living in the more and more AI-mediated world will become increasingly unlike us?
options: They will have lost the most significant human element of being intelligent.
They will no longer possess the human characteristic of being unpredictable.
They will not be able to understand themselves as we can do today.
They will be deprived of what their predecessors were proud of about themselves.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us.」
排除：A项“失去智慧”属无中生有；C项偏离“不可预测”这一特征；D项“前人骄傲之处”未提及。
q5.stemCn: 作者为什么说，生活在日益人工智能化世界里的生物将变得越来越不像我们？
optionsCn: 他们将失去作为智能这一最重要的人类特质。
他们将不再拥有不可预测这一人类特征。
他们将无法像我们今天这样理解自己。
他们将被剥夺其前辈们引以为傲的东西。

items.cn:
技术从来都不是实现人类目的的中立工具。技术创新在人们利用这些创新来控制环境的同时，也重塑了人类自身。例如，人工智能正在改变人性。
虽然人工智能这个术语让人联想到对杀人机器人或灾难性失业水平的担忧，但还有其他更深层次的含义。随着人工智能日益塑造人类体验，这如何改变"成为人类"的意义？问题的核心在于一个人做出选择的能力，特别是那些具有道德含义的判断。
亚里士多德认为，做出实践判断的能力依赖于定期做出这些判断——即习惯和实践。我们看到机器在各种日常情境中作为替代判断者的出现，这对人们学习如何有效运用自己的判断能力构成了潜在威胁。
在工作场所，管理者例行做出关于雇佣或解雇谁以及批准哪些贷款等决策。这些是算法性规定正在取代人类判断的领域，因此那些本有机会在这些领域发展实践判断能力的人将不再有这种机会。
推荐引擎作为人们在文化消费中日益普遍的中介，可能会限制选择并减少偶然性。通过向消费者展示算法选择的接下来要观看、阅读、流媒体访问和参观的内容，公司正在用机器品味取代人类品味。从某种意义上说，这是有帮助的。毕竟，机器可以比任何个人可能拥有的时间和精力更广泛地浏览选择范围。
然而，与此同时，这种选择是基于人们过去可能喜欢的内容来优化他们可能喜欢的内容。我们认为存在某种风险，即人们的选择将以一种新的、意想不到的方式被他们的过去所限制。
随着机器学习算法的改进和它们在更广泛数据集上的训练，日常生活的更大部分可能会变得完全可预测。预测会越来越好，最终将使常见体验更加高效和愉快。
算法很快就会——如果还没有的话——比你自己更清楚你接下来想看什么节目以及应该雇佣哪个求职者。有一天，人类甚至可能找到一种方法，让机器在做出这些决策时避免人类通常表现出的一些偏见。
但就不可预测性是人们理解自己的一部分以及人们喜欢自己特质的一部分而言，人类正在失去一些重要的东西。随着它们变得越来越可预测，生活在日益人工智能化世界中的生物将变得越来越不像我们。

items.text:
Phonics, which involves sounding out words _syllable_ (音节) by syllable, is the best way to teach children to read.But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. Most American children are taught to read in a way that study after study has found to be wrong.
The consequences of this are striking. Less than half of all American adults were proficient readers in 2017. American fourth graders rank 15th on the Progress in International Literacy Study, an international exam.
America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships (the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck, or ch), known as phonics. Others support an immersive approach (using pictures of a cat to learn the word cat), known as “whole language . Most teachers today, almost three out of four according to a survey by the EdWeek Research Centre in 2019, use a mix called "balanced literacy". This combination of methods is ineffective. "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics, says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. “It has to be systematic and explicitly taught."
Mississippi, often behind in social policy, has set an example here. In a state once notorious for its low reading scores, the Mississippi state legislature passed new literacy standards in 2013. Since then Mississippi has seen remarkable gains. Its fourth graders have moved from 49th (out of 50 states) to 29th on the National Assessment of Educational Progress, a nationwide exam. In 2019 it was the only state to improve its scores. For the first time since measurement began, Mississippi's pupils are now average readers, a remarkable achievement in such a poor state.
Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading. In 1997 Congress requested the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and the Department of Education to convene a National Reading Panel to end the “reading wars and synthesize the evidence. The panel found that phonics, along with explicit instruction in _phonemic_ (音位的) awareness, fluency and comprehension, worked best.
Yet over two decades on, “balanced literacy” is still being taught in classrooms. But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method. To the teacher who is a proficient reader, literacy seems like a natural process that requires educated guessing, rather than the deliberate process emphasized by phonics. Teachers can imagine that they learned to read through _osmosis_ (潜移默化) when they were children. Without proper training, they bring this to classrooms.

q5.stem: What do we learn about phonics in many American classrooms?
options: It is ill reputed.
It is mostly misapplied.
It is arbitrarily excluded.
It is misrepresented.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom.」
排除：B：错换主语，原文指教学方法错误，非 phonics 被误用；C：无中生有，未说 phonics 被任意排除；D：过度推断，未说 phonics 被歪曲表述
q5.stemCn: 在许多美国教室里，我们对自然拼读法了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它名声不佳。
它主要被误用。
它被任意排除。
它被歪曲。

q5.stem: What has America been witnessing for decades?
options: An obsession with innovating teaching methodologies of reading.
An enduring debate over the approach to teaching children to read.
An increasing concern with many children's inadequacy in literacy.
An ever-forceful advocacy of a combined method for teaching reading.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades.」
排除：A：长期存在的是争论而非痴迷创新，偷换概念；C：文提阅读后果，未说数十年日益担忧，无中生有；D：混合方法被批无效，非强力倡导，与原文不符
q5.stemCn: 美国几十年来一直在见证什么？
optionsCn: 对创新阅读教学方法的痴迷。
关于教孩子阅读方法的持久争论。
对许多儿童读写能力不足日益增长的担忧。
对综合阅读教学方法的日益有力的倡导。

q5.stem: Why does Tenette Smith think a combination of teaching methods is ineffective?
options: Elementary school children will be frustrated when taught with several methods combined.
Phonics has to be systematically applied and clearly taught to achieve the desired effect.
Sprinkling in a little phonics deters the progress of even adequately motivated children.
Balanced literacy fails to sustain children's interest in developing a good reading habit.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「“It has to be systematic and explicitly taught.」
排除：A：原文未提学生挫败感，属无中生有；C：将“不能点缀”误解为阻碍动机好的儿童，偷换概念；D：原文未提阅读习惯或兴趣，属无中生有。
q5.stemCn: 为什么特内特·史密斯认为教学方法的组合是无效的？
optionsCn: 当使用多种方法结合教学时，小学生会感到沮丧。
为了达到预期的效果，自然拼读法必须被系统地应用和清晰地教授。
在教学中穿插一点自然拼读法，甚至会阻碍那些动机充足的儿童的进步。
平衡读写能力未能维持儿童在培养良好阅读习惯方面的兴趣。

q5.stem: What does the author say Mississippi's success is attributed to?
options: Convening a National Reading Panel to synthesize research evidence.
Placing sufficient emphasis upon both fluency and comprehension.
Adopting scientifically grounded approaches to teaching reading.
Obtaining support from Congress to upgrade teaching methods.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading.」
排除：A：偷换概念，召集研究小组非成功原因；B：无中生有，原文未提两者为重点；D：张冠李戴，国会要求研究非该州成功因
q5.stemCn: 作者认为密西西比州的成功归因于什么？
optionsCn: 召集一个国家阅读小组以综合研究证据。
同时给予流利性和理解能力足够的重视。
采用有科学依据的教授阅读的方法。
获得国会对升级教学方法的支持。

q5.stem: What have advances in statistics and brain imaging proved ineffective?
options: The teaching of symbol-sound relationships.
Explicit instruction in phonemic awareness.
Efforts to end the reading wars.
The immersive approach.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method.」
排除：A：偷换概念，符号音关系即phonics，被证明有效。；B：张冠李戴，音位意识显性教学，被证明有效。；C：无中生有，结束阅读战争，并非被证无效。
q5.stemCn: 统计学和脑成像技术的进步证明了什么方法是无效的？
optionsCn: 符号与声音关系的教学。
对音位意识的明确指导。
结束“阅读战争”的努力。
沉浸式教学法。

items.cn:
自然拼读法，即逐音节发音的方法，是教孩子阅读的最佳方式。但在许多教室里，这可能是一个"脏话"。以至于一些教师不得不偷偷将自然拼读教学材料带入教室。大多数美国孩子所接受的阅读教学方法，被一项又一项的研究证明是错误的。
其后果令人震惊。2017年，不到一半的美国成年人是熟练的阅读者。在国际阅读进步研究（一项国际考试）中，美国四年级学生排名第15位。
美国陷入了一场关于儿童阅读教学的争论，这场争论已经持续了几十年。一些人提倡教授符号与声音的关系（k的发音可以拼写为c、k、ck或ch），这被称为自然拼读法。另一些人则支持沉浸式方法（用猫的图片来学习单词cat），这被称为"整体语言法"。如今大多数教师，根据2019年EdWeek研究中心的调查，近四分之三使用一种被称为"平衡读写"的混合方法。这种方法的组合是无效的。"你不能只是零星地加入一点自然拼读，"密西西比州教育厅小学教育和阅读执行主任Tenette Smith说。"它必须是系统性的和明确教授的。"
密西西比州在社会政策方面常常落后，但在这里树立了榜样。在这个曾经以阅读分数低而闻名的州，密西西比州立法机构在2013年通过了新的读写标准。自那时以来，密西西比州取得了显著进步。在全国教育进步评估（一项全国性考试）中，该州四年级学生从第49位（50个州中）上升到第29位。2019年，它是唯一一个分数有所提高的州。自测量开始以来，密西西比州的学生首次成为平均水平的阅读者，在这个如此贫困的州，这是一个非凡的成就。
密西西比州的成功归功于实施了一项被称为"阅读科学"的研究所支持的阅读方法。1997年，国会要求国家儿童健康与人类发展研究所和教育部召集一个全国阅读小组，以结束"阅读战争"并综合证据。该小组发现，自然拼读法，加上对音位意识、流利性和理解力的明确教学，效果最好。
然而，二十多年过去了，"平衡读写"仍然在教室里教授。但统计学和脑成像技术的进步已经证明整体语言法是错误的。对于熟练的阅读者教师来说，读写似乎是一个需要合理猜测的自然过程，而不是自然拼读法所强调的有意识的过程。教师们可能会想象他们小时候是通过潜移默化学会阅读的。没有适当的培训，他们就把这种方法带到了教室。

items.text:
How on earth did we come to this? We protect our children obsessively from every harm; we scrutinize every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact. Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.
We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children. Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity, or learned to handle money, they're encouraged to associate status and self-worth with stuff, and to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation. We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.
We've reached this point so gradually that many of us have never questioned it. It's crept up on us in the 60 years since advertisers started to target the young and found that they could recruit them to a commercial assault on their parents. We've come to know it as“pester power"or the ability of children to pressure parents to make certain purchases.
Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.
Not all psychologists agree. There're plenty working hand in glove with a f12bn-a-year industry that has turned the manipulation of adult emotions and desires into an art form — often literally. It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements'viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many. Advertising and marketing can serve a useful purpose for children. Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products, and help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood.
Then, should we ban all advertising aimed at young children? I say yes.
Of course there'll be plenty of objections to an outright ban on advertising to the under-11s. There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.
Most parents hate what advertising does to their children, but we do have the power to end it and let our children grow up free from many of the pressures of consumerism until they're old enough to make their own decisions. And though advertising is only part of an _all-pervasive_ (无处不在的) marketing culture we need to make a start somewhere. Let's ban all advertising targeting children of primary school age and younger now.

q5.stem: Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children?
options: Advertisers.
Carers.
Teachers.
Doctors.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.
We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children.」
排除：B：carers属被细查群体，张冠李戴，非目标；C：teachers属被细查群体，张冠李戴，非目标；D：doctors属被细查群体，张冠李戴，非目标
q5.stemCn: 作者指出哪一类人拥有几乎不受限制的接触儿童的权限？
optionsCn: 广告商
照顾者
教师
医生

q5.stem: What kind of people should we enable children to become according to the author?
options: Those who look to fame and wealth for external and ultimate validation.
Those who value themselves because of their contribution to society.
Those who associate self-worth with the ability to handle money.
Those who have developed a proper sense of their own identity.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.」
排除：A：这是作者批判的倾向，与原文相反；C：理财能力非自我价值来源，偷换概念；D：身份认同只是前提，非作者期望目标，范围错位
q5.stemCn: 根据作者的观点，我们应该让孩子成为什么样的人？
optionsCn: 那些从名望和财富中寻求外在且最终认可的人。
那些因为自己对社会的贡献而看重自己的人。
那些将自我价值与处理金钱的能力联系起来的人。
那些形成了恰当的自我身份感的人。

q5.stem: Many child development experts and educators call attention to research that suggests
options: life-long consumerism is causing more and more cases of psychological problems.
increasing commercialization of education is eroding many children's self-esteem.
the growing desire for wealth is contributing to a rising rate of depression.
the craving for purchasing material things is nurtured throughout one's life.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.」
排除：B：原文未提教育商业化，属无中生有。；C：抑郁由消费主义引起，非财富欲望，张冠李戴。；D：只说终身消费致病，未论消费欲如何被培养，偏题。
q5.stemCn: 许多儿童发展专家和教育学家呼吁人们关注一项研究，该研究表明
optionsCn: 终身的消费主义正导致越来越多的心理问题。
教育日益商业化正在侵蚀许多孩子的自尊心。
日益增长的财富欲望正在导致抑郁率的上升。
对购买物质事物的渴望贯穿人的一生。

q5.stem: What does the author imply about the impact of advertising?
options: It is actually infectious to many rather than a few.
It is rooted in our desire for material possessions.
It is comparable to that of virus.
It is literally limited to children.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements'viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many.」
排除：B：无中生有，原文说广告催生欲望，非欲望为根；C：偷换概念，病毒仅喻广告传播，非整体影响；D：范围过窄，原文还涉及成人被操纵
q5.stemCn: 作者对广告的影响有何暗示？
optionsCn: 它实际上对许多人而非少数人具有传染性。
它根植于我们对物质财富的渴望。
它可与病毒的影响相媲美。
它确实仅限于儿童。

q5.stem: What is the opponents'argument against a complete ban on advertising to young children?
options: It would deprive them of the chance to learn about products.
It would render them unable to carve out unique identities.
It would breach their freedom as would-be consumers.
It would violate the rights endowed upon advertisers.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.」
排除：A：把营销帮助儿童了解产品说成反对禁广理由，张冠李戴。；B：把营销帮助形成身份说成反对禁广理由，无中生有。；C：将广告商权利偷换成未来消费者自由，主体错误。
q5.stemCn: 反对者对全面禁止向儿童做广告的论点是什么？
optionsCn: 这会剥夺他们了解产品的机会。
这会使他们无法塑造独特的身份。
这会侵犯他们作为潜在消费者的自由。
这会侵犯赋予广告商的权利。

items.cn:
我们究竟是如何走到这一步的？我们 obsessive 地保护孩子免受一切伤害；我们仔细审查与他们接触的每一位护理人员、老师或医生。尽管如此，有一个群体，他们完全没有孩子的最佳利益放在心上，却几乎不受限制地接触孩子。
我们似乎想当然地认为，广告商和营销人员被允许 even the youngest children 进行 conditioning。在孩子们甚至还没有形成适当的自我意识，或者学会处理金钱之前，他们就被鼓励将地位和自我价值与物质联系起来，并寻求外部事物如名望和财富来获得认可。我们培养出的是小消费者，而不是年轻公民，这些年轻公民会因为他们对所生活的社会的贡献而珍视自己。
我们如此渐进地达到了这一点，以至于我们中的许多人从未质疑过它。在广告商开始针对年轻人并发现他们可以招募年轻人对父母进行商业攻击的60年里，它不知不觉地侵入了我们的生活。我们称之为"纠缠的力量"，即孩子们能够迫使父母购买某些商品的能力。
许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育者指出研究，表明这种从摇篮到坟墓的新兴消费主义正在助长低自尊、抑郁和其他形式精神疾病的增长。
并非所有心理学家都同意。有许多人与一个每年120亿英镑的行业密切合作，这个行业已经将操纵成年人的情感和欲望变成了一种艺术形式——有时是字面意义上的。这个行业还在不断开发新的方法来说服我们的孩子渴望物质财富，并且由于广告的病毒效应，他们只需要感染少数人就能影响多数人。广告和营销可以为儿童提供有用的目的。营销可能帮助儿童作为消费者社会化，让他们了解产品，并帮助他们形成独特的身份认同，当他们成年时。
那么，我们应该禁止所有针对年幼儿童的广告吗？我的答案是肯定的。
当然，对于完全禁止针对11岁以下儿童的广告，会有很多反对意见。会有一些人认为，这会侵犯言论自由，并侵犯公司洗脑小儿童以要求其产品的权利。
大多数父母讨厌广告对他们的孩子所做的事情，但我们确实有能力结束它，让我们的孩子在不受消费主义许多压力的情况下成长，直到他们足够大可以自己做决定。尽管广告只是无处不在的营销文化的一部分，但我们还是需要从某个地方开始。让我们现在禁止所有针对小学及以下年龄儿童的广告。

items.text:
Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. But it's on the rise around the world as firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers. More than half of companies with over $750m in annual revenue used “non-traditional”monitoring techniques on staff last year.
Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves. A growing number of analytics companies offer this service. They gather“data exhaust”left by employees'email and instant messaging apps, and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identification devices and microphones. These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations. While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.
Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.
Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular“chipping parties”, where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.
As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove to be detrimental. And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that's when they prove most unpopular. A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.
If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst. But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46%of employees are generally okay with it. Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain skeptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.
So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff and useful for companies looking to become more efficient and profitable. But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.

q5.stem: Why are many people opposed to monitoring employee performance?
options: It puts workers under constant pressure.
It is universally deemed anti-human by nature.
It does both mental and physical harm to employees monitored.
It enables firms to squeeze maximal productivity from employees.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings.」
排除：B：原文指内在去人性化，非普遍反人类，范围扩大；C：原文只提压力，未说身心伤害，属无中生有；D：企业榨取效率非反对原因，偷换因果
q5.stemCn: 为什么很多人反对监控员工绩效？
optionsCn: 它使员工持续处于压力之下。
它被普遍认为本质上反人性。
它对被监控的员工造成身心伤害。
它使公司能够从员工身上榨取最大生产力。

q5.stem: What is the supporters'argument for workplace surveillance?
options: It enables employees to refrain from dominating conversations.
It enhances employees'identification with firms they work in.
It can alert employees to intrusion into their privacy.
It can protect employees against aggressive behavior.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.」
排除：A：曲解原文，仅监测是否不主导对话，非让其避免主导。；B：无中生有，原文未提增强员工对公司的认同。；C：偷换概念，原文称可能侵扰隐私，非提醒员工隐私受侵。
q5.stemCn: 支持者对工作场所监控的论点是什么？
optionsCn: 它使员工能够避免主导谈话。
它增强了员工对所在公司的认同感。
它可以提醒员工注意对其隐私的侵犯。
它可以保护员工免受攻击性行为的伤害。

q5.stem: What does the author want to show by the example of different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables?
options: Data analysis is key to the successful implementation of workplace surveillance.
Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected.
More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing.
It is hard to decide on how many people to sit at a lunch table without data analysis.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results.」
排除：A：例子仅表明数据分析可产生意外发现，未证明它是成功实施的关键；C：该选项只是举例细节，非作者想说明的数据意外发现作用；D：无中生有，原文只说缺少分析会难发现事实，非难决定就座人数
q5.stemCn: 作者通过不同数量的人在午餐桌旁互动的例子想说明什么？
optionsCn: 数据分析是成功实施工作场所监控的关键。
分析从工人那里收集的数据可能会得出意想不到的结果。
更多的同事坐在一张午餐桌上往往会促进互动和思想交流。
没有数据分析，很难决定有多少人坐在一张午餐桌上。

q5.stem: What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?
options: How frequently employees are to be monitored.
What specific personal information is being excluded.
What steps are taken to minimize their detrimental impact.
How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst. But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46%of employees are generally okay with it.」
排除：A：频次未决定效果，无中生有；B：排除信息非条件，无中生有；C：减害步骤非依据，偷换概念
q5.stemCn: 监控举措的大部分积极效果取决于什么？
optionsCn: 员工被监控的频率。
哪些具体的个人信息被排除在外。
采取了哪些步骤来减少其不利影响。
老板们多大程度上阐明其监控的目的。

q5.stem: What concern do monitoring initiatives cause among many staffers?
options: They may empower employers excessively.
They may erode the workplace environment.
They may infringe upon staffers'entitled freedom.
They may become counterproductive in the long run.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain skeptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.」
排除：A：偷换概念，原文未说员工担心雇主权力过度膨胀；B：无中生有，未提破坏职场环境；D：偷换条件，错误实施才可能反生产
q5.stemCn: 许多员工对监控举措有何担忧？
optionsCn: 它们可能会过度地赋予雇主权力。
它们可能会侵蚀工作环境。
它们可能会侵犯员工应享有的自由。
从长远来看，它们可能会适得其反。

items.cn:
许多人反对工作场所的监控，因为它具有固有的非人化效应，并会带来持续不断的压力。但随着公司试图通过从员工身上榨取更高的生产力来提高效率，这种监控在全球范围内日益兴起。去年，年收入超过7.5亿美元的公司中，超过一半对员工使用了“非传统”的监控技术。
监控员工绩效使公司能够评估员工的表现和互动情况，这对公司和员工双方都有好处。越来越多的分析公司提供这项服务。他们收集员工电子邮件和即时通讯应用留下的“数据废气”，并使用配备射频识别设备和麦克风的名牌。这些设备可以检查你花多少时间说话，你的音量和语调，即使你没有主导对话。虽然这可能听起来很具侵入性，但支持者认为它也可以保护员工免受欺凌和性骚扰。
其中一些数据分析可能会产生意想不到的结果。例如，研究发现，坐在12人午餐桌旁的人倾向于更多地互动、分享想法，并且表现优于那些经常坐在四人桌旁的人，如果没有这样的数据分析，这个事实可能不会被察觉。
在过去几年里，斯德哥尔摩一个名为Epicenter的共享办公空间走得更远，并举办受欢迎的“植入芯片派对”，人们可以在那里将微芯片植入手中。他们可以使用这些植入物来进入电子控制门，或者监控打字速度与心率的相关性。植入芯片可能看起来很极端，但从身份证和生物识别技术到这类设备，只是一小步。
只要这些计划是自愿的，可能会有越来越多的以便利为导向的用途，以至于大量员工会选择植入芯片。但如果植入芯片被用来减少空闲时间或休息时间，那可能会证明是有害的。而且，如果监控工具剥夺了员工的自主性，那时它们就会变得最不受欢迎。这很大程度上取决于这类监控倡议如何被传达，并且这可以防止可能发生的反抗。
如果老板们不能有效地沟通，员工会往最坏处想。但如果他们对所收集的信息及其用途保持透明，研究表明，46%的员工对此大体上持接受态度。尽管许多此类监控计划使用匿名数据且参与是自愿的，许多员工仍然持怀疑态度，并担心他们的公民自由会受到侵蚀。
因此，工作场所监控可能对员工赋权，并且对寻求变得更高效、更盈利的公司有用。但如果实施方式不当，它也可能成为一个不受欢迎的压迫工具，并且证明是适得其反的。

items.text:
If you're someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the _pandemic_ (大流行病), you're not alone. Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies'aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health. In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants'efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they're responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates.
Processed food is inexpensive, it's legal, and it's everywhere. Companies'advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly. So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people. Memory, _nostalgia_ (怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave. Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they're at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment. Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they're going to think of soda. Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood.
Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking.
One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory. What we eat is all about memory. And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age. And we keep those memories for a lifetime. Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively. There's nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain. For Moss, this puts the notion of “fast food” in an entirely new light as this isn't limited to fast food chains — almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods. Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.
Overall, Moss outlines the industry's dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers. Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.

q5.stem: In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes?
options: They are all addictive.
They are all necessary evils.
They are all engineered to be enjoyed.
They are all in increasingly great demand.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances.」
排除：B：无中生有，原文未称它们为“必要的恶”。；C：偷换概念，“hook you”指令人上瘾，非旨在被享受。；D：无中生有，原文未说三者需求都在不断增长。
q5.stemCn: 迈克尔·莫斯认为加工食品与酒精和香烟有何相似之处？
optionsCn: 它们都是令人上瘾的。
它们都是必要的恶。
它们都是为了让人享受而经过精心设计的。
它们的需求量都越来越大。

q5.stem: What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave?
options: The food environment.
Aggressive marketing.
Convenience.
Memory.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Memory, _nostalgia_ (怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave.」
排除：A：食品环境只指问题食物环境，非渴望主因。；B：书论营销，但原句未说营销是关键。；C：便利只是行业依赖之一，非所问。
q5.stemCn: 作者说在我们渴望的食物中起关键作用的是什么？
optionsCn: 食物环境。
积极的营销。
便利性。
记忆。

q5.stem: What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers'association with their food products?
options: They strive to influence how consumers remember their products.
They attempt to use consumers'long-term memories to promote addiction.
They try to exploit consumers'memories for their products as early as possible.
They endeavor to find what consumers remember about their products.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products.」
排除：B：无中生有，原文未说用长期记忆促进成瘾；C：曲解原文，早期形成记忆不等于最早利用；D：偷换概念，原文是塑造记忆而非查找记忆
q5.stemCn: 食品公司为了利用消费者对其食品产品的联想，会怎么做？
optionsCn: 他们努力影响消费者对其产品的记忆方式。
他们试图利用消费者的长期记忆来促进成瘾。
他们尝试尽早地利用消费者对其产品的记忆。
他们致力于找出消费者对其产品的记忆内容。

q5.stem: How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss?
options: Placing the idea of fast food in an entirely new light.
Setting no limit to the number of fast food chains.
Focusing on how quickly the work is done.
Prioritizing the quality of their products.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.」
排除：A：把“快食品新角度”当操作方式，属偷换概念；B：原文说不仅限快餐连锁，非无数量限制，属曲解；D：原文强调速度便捷，未说优先质量，属无中生有
q5.stemCn: 根据莫斯的说法，食品行业是如何从生产到包装进行运作的？
optionsCn: 将快餐的理念置于一个全新的视角下。
对快餐连锁店的数量不设限。
专注于工作完成的速度。
优先考虑他们产品的质量。

q5.stem: Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers'demand for healthier food products?
options: They think speed of production outweighs consumers'health.
They believe their industry would perish without fast foods.
They have to strike a balance between taste and nutrition.
They are hooked on manufacturing convenience foods.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.」
排除：A：偷换概念，未称速度重于健康。；B：无中生有，未称无快餐业会亡。；C：曲解原文，非口味营养平衡。
q5.stemCn: 为什么公司发现很难满足消费者对更健康食品产品的需求？
optionsCn: 他们认为生产速度比消费者的健康更重要。
他们相信，如果没有快餐，他们的行业将会消亡。
他们必须在味道和营养之间取得平衡。
他们沉迷于制造方便食品。

items.cn:
如果你是在大流行病期间更倾向于吃垃圾食品的人，你并非孤例。调查记者迈克尔·莫斯说，加工食品的设计就是为了让你上瘾，这与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质并无二致。他2013年的著作《盐、糖、脂肪》探讨了食品公司对这些产品的激进营销及其对我们健康的影响。在他新书《上瘾》中，莫斯更新了食品巨头们让我们持续食用他们所提供产品的努力，以及他们如何应对消费者和健康倡导者的投诉。
加工食品价格低廉、合法合规，并且无处不在。公司的广告在提醒我们记住这些产品，让我们不断地渴望它们。因此，食品环境是导致食物对许多人来说问题更严重的关键因素之一。记忆，尤其是怀旧情绪，在我们渴望的食物中扮演着重要角色。汽水公司发现，如果他们在孩子与父母一起观看棒球比赛时，将一罐汽水递到孩子手中，那罐汽水将永远与那个快乐的时刻联系在一起。日后，当那个孩子想要体验快乐的时刻时，他们会想到汽水。许多人从童年记忆中的零食中寻求慰藉。
莫斯研究了公司如何利用我们的记忆、渴望和大脑化学物质来让我们持续吃零食。
我认为这些食品产品甚至比毒品更具威力、更令人担忧的原因之一，就是记忆。我们所吃的一切都与记忆有关。我们在非常年幼的时候就开始为食物形成记忆，而这些记忆我们会保持一生。了解了这一点，食品行业花费大量时间试图塑造我们对他们产品的记忆。研究药物成瘾的科学家在20世纪90年代发现，成瘾的一个特征是：物质进入大脑的速度越快，我们就越容易因此冲动行事。在作用于大脑的速度方面，没有什么比食物更快了。对莫斯而言，这给“快餐”的概念带来了全新的视角，因为这一点不仅限于快餐连锁店——杂货店里近90%的食品都是加工食品。从生产到包装，这个行业的一切都关乎速度。
总而言之，莫斯概述了该行业对使其产品价格低廉、超级美味和极其便利给消费者的依赖。如今，随着越来越多的人关心他们摄入的东西并希望吃得健康，这些公司发现，由于自身对生产这些便利食品的依赖，他们很难满足这一新的需求。

items.text:
_Chimpanzees_ (黑猩猩), human beings'closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes. Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives. Fewer than 300, 000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe. At more than 7 billion, human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals — despite our physical weaknesses.
What could account for our species'incredible evolutionary successes?
One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.
But a growing number of cognitive scientists and _anthropologists_ (人类学家) are rejecting that explanation. They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.
In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects-children and chimpanzees — a mechanical box with a treat inside. In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent. The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick.
Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally:Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.
Of course, that study only included three-and four-year-olds. But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others'actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate — that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions.
By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition. In the transparent condition — where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless — they ignored that step entirely. Other research has since supported these findings.
When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults.
Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from?Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.
So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. We're not chimpanzees, after all.

q5.stem: What might explain humans'having the largest population of almost all mammals?
options: They are equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems.
They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives.
They possess the most outstanding ability to think.
They know how to survive everywhere on earth.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.」
排除：A：偷换概念，智力≠原始体力；B：无中生有，未说比亲属更有效；D：答非所问，仅生存结果，非原因。
q5.stemCn: 什么可以解释人类在几乎所有哺乳动物中拥有最大的种群数量？
optionsCn: 他们拥有解决最具挑战性问题的强大能力。
他们比自己的动物亲戚更有效地应对外部世界。
他们拥有最杰出的思考能力。
他们知道如何在地球上的任何地方生存。

q5.stem: What accounts for humans'evolutionary successes according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists?
options: They are better at innovating solutions.
They thrive through creative strategies.
They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts.
They meet challenges by imitating others carefully.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.」
排除：A：被原文否定，并非靠创新；B：与原文相反，非创意策略；C：无中生有，靠复制应对。
q5.stemCn: 越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家认为，是什么解释了人类在进化上的成功？
optionsCn: 他们更擅长创新解决方案。
他们通过创造性的策略蓬勃发展。
他们天生适应生态环境。
他们通过仔细模仿他人来应对挑战。

q5.stem: What does the author think is odd about the findings of the study by Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten?
options: Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters.
Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one.
Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did.
Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally:Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.」
排除：B：原文未说黑猩猩区分透明与不透明盒子；C：无速度比较；D：与原文相反，儿童未省略步骤。
q5.stemCn: 作者认为维多利亚·霍纳和安德鲁·怀顿的研究发现有什么奇怪之处？
optionsCn: 儿童不合逻辑地模仿了实验者的每一个动作。
黑猩猩能够分辨透明的盒子和不透明的那个。
黑猩猩比孩子们更快地拿到了奖赏。
儿童省略了用棍子敲击盒子来打开它的步骤。

q5.stem: What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying?
options: It originates in the rationality of people around the world.
It stems from the way people learn complex technologies.
It results from people distrusting their own wisdom.
It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally.」
排除：A：人类靠非理性学习复杂技术，未说源自全球理性；C：强调信任更有经验者，未说不信任自身智慧；D：逐步学习是结果，非出于获取知识的欲望。
q5.stemCn: 人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇对人类偏好模仿的解释是什么？
optionsCn: 它源于世界各地人们的理性。
它源于人们学习复杂技术的方式。
它源于人们不信任自己的智慧。
它源于一步步获取知识的愿望。

q5.stem: What point does the author want to emphasize when he says “We're not chimpanzees”?
options: It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation.
It is characteristic of human beings to copy others.
It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers.
It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.」
排除：A：非重点，原文强调人类爱模仿，非‘是否应避免模仿’存争议；C：过度引申，原文仅说学习技术需信任长者，非题眼；D：曲解最后建议，原文是笑‘避免模仿’者，非笑拥抱非从众
q5.stemCn: 当作者说“我们不是黑猩猩”时，他想强调什么观点？
optionsCn: 是否每个人都应该避免模仿，这一点值得商榷。
模仿他人是人类的特点。
信任更有知识的同龄人是可取的。
嘲笑那些拥抱非主流的人是幼稚的。

items.cn:
黑猩猩，人类最亲近的动物亲戚，与我们共享高达98%的基因。然而，人类和黑猩猩的生活却截然不同。如今，不到30万只野生黑猩猩生活在非洲少数几个森林角落，而人类却已殖民地球的每一个角落。人类人口超过70亿，远超几乎所有其他哺乳动物——尽管我们在身体上存在弱点。
是什么解释了我们物种令人难以置信的进化成功？
一个明显的答案是我们的大脑。可能是我们的原始智能赋予了我们前所未有的跳出思维定式的能力，随着人们在全球范围内迁徙，不断创新解决棘手问题的方法。
但越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家正在拒绝这种解释。他们认为，我们之所以生存和繁荣，恰恰不是因为我们是创新者，而是因为我们不独立思考。相反，人们通过仔细模仿他人来应对具有挑战性的气候和生态环境。
在一项著名的研究中，心理学家维多利亚·霍纳和安德鲁·怀特向两组测试对象——儿童和黑猩猩——展示了一个装有奖励的机械盒子。在一种情况下，盒子是不透明的，而在另一种情况下则是透明的。实验者展示了如何打开盒子取出奖励，但他们还包括了一个用棍子敲打盒子的无关步骤。
奇怪的是，孩子们仔细复制了打开盒子的所有步骤，即使他们能看到棍子没有实际效果。也就是说，他们不合理地模仿：为了获得奖励，孩子们不仅只做必要的事情，而是盲目地模仿他们目睹的每一个动作。
当然，该研究只包括三岁和四岁的儿童。但进一步的研究表明，年龄较大的儿童和成年人更可能盲目地模仿他人的行为，而婴儿则不太可能过度模仿——也就是说，他们不太可能精确地复制甚至不切实际的动作。
相比之下，研究中的黑猩猩只在盒子不透明的情况下过度模仿。在透明的情况下——当他们看到棍子在机械上无用时——他们完全忽略了那个步骤。其他研究此后也支持了这些发现。
在模仿方面，黑猩猩比人类儿童或成年人更理性。
人类对过度模仿的看似不合理偏好从何而来？人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇指出，世界各地的人们依赖的技术往往非常复杂，没有人能够理性地学习它们。相反，人们必须一步一步地学习它们，信任更有经验的年长者和同伴的智慧。
所以，下次当你听到有人热情地争论说每个人都应该拥抱非从众主义并避免模仿他人时，你可能会笑一笑。毕竟，我们不是黑猩猩。

items.text:
One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts.
The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.
Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans.
This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages.
Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks.
Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.
Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production — he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too.
The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.
Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces. The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none.
It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise.
In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
A focus on wage growth would provide an _antidote_ (矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.

q5.stem: Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective?
options: Its critics' voice has not been heard throughout the country.
There seem to be no other options available to replace it.
The cult of tax cuts has been relentlessly propagated by all policymakers.
There appears to be a misunderstanding of the formula among the public.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.」
排除：A：原文称批评者众多，“未被听到”无中生有且与原文相反；C：“所有政策制定者”扩大范围，原文仅共和党等，无中生有；D：原文未提公众误解，属无中生有。
q5.stemCn: 为什么减税方案尽管无效却依然受欢迎？
optionsCn: 批评者的声音在全国范围内没有被听到。
似乎没有其他可用的选项来替代它。
减税崇拜被所有政策制定者不懈地传播。
在公众之中似乎对该方案存在误解。

q5.stem: What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.?
options: Aiding people left behind by economic growth.
Prioritizing the growth of the nation's GDP.
Increasing the compensation for labor.
Introducing even more extensive tax cuts.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.」
排除：A：张冠李戴；民主党助落后者，非作者增长措施。；B：与原文相反；作者主张少盯GDP，非优先GDP。；D：与原文相反；减税公式无效，非更有效措施。
q5.stemCn: 作者认为，在美国，推动经济增长的更有效措施是什么？
optionsCn: 帮助经济增长中的落伍者。
优先考虑国家GDP的增长。
提高劳动报酬。
实施更大规模的减税。

q5.stem: What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?
options: The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy.
Paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce attracts more customers.
Consumption stimulates the desire for higher wages.
Familiar arguments for higher wages are outdated.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.」
排除：B：Ford案例细节，非整体逻辑；C：因果颠倒，涨薪促消费；D：无中生有，未称公平论过时
q5.stemCn: 作者观点背后的逻辑是什么？
optionsCn: 工人工资的增长最终会推动国家经济。
支付溢价以维持可靠的员工队伍，能吸引更多顾客。
消费刺激了对更高工资的渴望。
支持提高工资的常见论点已经过时了。

q5.stem: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom?
options: Fairness in distribution.
Increase in productivity.
The priority of economic policymakers.
The unerring judgment of market forces.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages.」
排除：A：作者搁置“公平”论证，非传统共识依据；C：工资优先是作者主张，非传统共识依据；D：市场力量决定薪酬是主流观点，非传统共识依据
q5.stemCn: 根据传统观念，更高工资的基础是什么？
optionsCn: 分配的公平性。
生产力的提高。
经济政策制定者的优先事项。
市场力量的无误判断。

q5.stem: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?
options: People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity.
People have been disheartened by the widening gap between the haves and have-nots.
People have witnessed a tug of war between Republicans and Democrats over tax cuts.
People have seen the link disappearing between productivity and workers' well-being.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.」
排除：A：原文指生产率与工资增长背离，非未能看到二者同步增长；B：原文指生产率与工资增长差距，未提贫富差距或民众情绪；C：原文是劳资博弈，不是两党围绕减税的博弈
q5.stemCn: 在过去50年左右的时间里，我们从美国现实世界中的事情中了解到什么？
optionsCn: 人们未能看到工资和生产力的相应增长。
人们因富人与穷人之间日益扩大的差距而感到沮丧。
人们目睹了共和党与民主党之间围绕减税的拉锯战。
人们看到生产力与工人福祉之间的联系正在消失。

items.cn:
近几十年来，共和党的一大成功之处在于不懈地传播一个简单的经济增长公式：减税。
这个公式并不奏效，但这并未影响其受欢迎程度。尽管减税狂热已经吸引了众多批评者，但它却缺乏明显的竞争对手。
民主党政治家们倾向于竞选时承诺帮助那些被经济增长抛在后面的人。当民主党人确实谈论鼓励经济增长时，他们听起来常常像共和党人。
这不仅对民主党是一个政治问题；对美国来说也是一个经济问题。这个国家需要一个关于经济增长驱动因素更好的叙事。近几十年的痛苦教训指向了一个有希望的候选者：更高的工资。
提高美国工人的工资应该是经济政策制定者的优先事项。我们都应该少关注国家国内生产总值（GDP）增长的季度更新，而更多地关注工人工资的增长。
暂时搁置关于提高工资的熟悉论点：公平性。这里的论点是，更高的工资可以为经济增长的引擎提供燃料。
关于好处的最著名的例证或许是亨利·福特在1914年决定为T型装配线工人每天支付5美元工资的故事。他这样做是为了提高产量——他支付溢价以维持一支可靠的劳动力队伍。意想不到的好处是，福特的工厂工人也成为了福特的顾客。
同样的逻辑仍然适用：消费驱动美国经济，而获得更高报酬的工人可以消费更多。
主流经济学家坚持认为，不可能命令实现工资的可持续增长，因为薪酬水平反映了市场力量的准确判断。传统观点认为，生产率增长是提高工资的唯一途径。从这个角度来看，努力争取提高工资是适得其反的。最低工资法会增加失业，因为工资池中的资金是有限的，如果一些人得到更多，其他人就会一无所获。
正是在这种世界观背景下，减税将促进繁荣的观点变得流行起来。富人会投资，生产率会提高，工资也会上涨。
在现实世界中，事情要复杂得多。工资受到雇主和工人之间拉锯战的影响，而雇主一直占据上风。一个明确的证据是自大约1970年以来生产率增长和工资增长之间差距的扩大。生产率已经翻了一番多；工资远远落后。
关注工资增长将为减税神奇力量的信念提供一种有吸引力的简单性的矫正方法。

items.text:
Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.
Unfortunately, a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.
Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.
The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience — a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.
Based on their results, the team concludes that “the ideas, values, and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience.”
Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.
This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants — the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.
A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.

q5.stem: What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities?
options: Insight.
Expertise
Integrity.
Diversity.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.」
排除：A：无中生有，原文未要求编辑部体现洞察力；B：偷换概念，原文强调多样声音而非专业能力；C：无中生有，原文未论及编辑的正直品质
q5.stemCn: 鉴于其重要的责任，我们期望一份学术期刊的编辑委员会展现出什么？
optionsCn: 洞察力。
专业知识
正直。
多样性。

q5.stem: What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience?
options: The majority of top psychology and neuroscience journals reflect a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.
The editorial boards of most psychology and neuroscience journals do influence the direction their field takes.
The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male-dominated.
The majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals have relevant backgrounds.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.」
排除：A：与原文相反，编辑多为男性，并非多样身份；B：非研究发现，属于开篇一般论述；D：偷换概念，原文仅指来自美国，非相关背景
q5.stemCn: 我们从《自然·神经科学》的一项新研究中能了解到什么？
optionsCn: 大多数顶尖的心理学和神经科学期刊都反映了多样化的声音、经验和身份。
大多数心理学和神经科学期刊的编辑委员会确实会影响其领域的发展方向。
心理学和神经科学领域最重要期刊的编辑委员会由男性主导。
顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑拥有相关的背景。

q5.stem: What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals?
options: There were quite a few female editors who also distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers.
The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research.
The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels.
There were few female editors who could move up to senior positions.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.」
排除：A：无中生有，未提女性编辑也是权威研究者；C：曲解原文，未说资深层级比例更低；D：过度推断，未提能晋升女性少。
q5.stemCn: 作者在心理学期刊编辑的性别差异方面强调了什么事实？
optionsCn: 有相当多的女性编辑也成为了有影响力的心理学研究者。
女性编辑的数量与从事心理学研究的女性人数不成比例。
在高级别职位上，女性编辑的比例越来越低。
很少有女性编辑能够晋升到高级职位。

q5.stem: What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings?
options: Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals.
Male editors of top psychology and neuroscience journals tend to be biased against their female colleagues.
Male researchers have enough representation in the editorial boards to ensure their publications.
Female editors have to struggle to get women's research articles published in academic journals.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Based on their results, the team concludes that “the ideas, values, and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience.”」
排除：B：无中生有，男性编辑偏见过强不等于歧视女同事；C：过度推断，男性代表多不能推出确保其发表；D：无中生有，未提女编辑艰难发表女性论文
q5.stemCn: 根据新研究团队的发现，我们可以从他们的结论中推断出什么？
optionsCn: 在顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的编辑委员会中，女性的观点代表性不足。
顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的男性编辑往往对他们的女性同事有偏见。
男性研究者在编辑委员会中有足够的代表性，以确保他们的研究成果能够发表。
女性编辑不得不努力争取让女性的研究文章在学术期刊上发表。

q5.stem: What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition?
options: Strike a balance between male and female editors.
Increase women's employment in senior positions.
Enlarge the body of female academics.
Implement overall structural reforms.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.」
排除：A：强调平衡性别比例，未涉及破除结构性障碍；B：增加高层女性只是传统解释，与作者观点相悖；C：原文称女性学者数量不足并非问题
q5.stemCn: 作者建议我们做什么，而不是仅仅将编辑委员会的不平等归咎于传统？
optionsCn: 在男女编辑之间取得平衡。
增加女性在高级职位上的就业。
扩大女性学者的群体。
实施全面的结构性改革。

items.cn:
期刊编辑决定发表什么内容、不发表什么内容，影响着其他学者的职业生涯，并影响着一个领域的发展方向。因此，人们会希望期刊尽一切努力建立一个多元化的编辑委员会，反映多样化的声音、经验和身份。
不幸的是，发表在《自然·神经科学》上的一项新研究读来令人沮丧。研究团队发现，顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑都是男性，并且都位于美国：这种情况可能正在加剧该领域现有的性别不平等，并影响着发表的研究类型。
研究发现，男性占心理学期刊编辑的60%。在各个资历级别上，男性编辑都显著多于女性编辑，并且在超过四分之三的期刊中，男性占编辑多数。关键的是，女性编辑的比例显著低于女性心理学研究者的总体比例。
在神经科学期刊中，差异更为显著：70%的编辑是男性，并且在88%的期刊中，男性占据大多数编辑职位。在这种情况下，女性编辑的比例与神经科学领域女性研究者的比例相比并没有显著降低——这一发现揭示了该领域更广泛的持续性别差异。
基于研究结果，研究团队得出结论："在心理学和神经科学领域最知名的学术期刊的编辑职位中，男性的观点、价值观和决策偏见被过度代表了。"
科学领域的性别不平等通常归因于高级学者更可能是男性这一事实，因为历史上科学领域由男性主导：有人认为随着时间的推移，随着更多女性担任高级职位，该领域将变得更加平等。然而，这项研究表明，尽管实际上初级心理学教职中女性多于男性，但心理学期刊的初级职位仍然倾向于由男性不成比例地占据。
这意味着缺乏女性学者不是问题所在。相反，存在结构性原因导致女性在科学领域处于不利地位。例如，女性获得较低的薪酬，面临更大的育儿需求，这可能导致发表成果和获得资助减少——而这些正是期刊在决定任命人选时所看重的因素。我们不应简单地将编辑委员会的不平等归咎于传统，而应积极打破这些现有的障碍。
期刊编辑缺乏多样性也可能导致心理学领域的"WEIRD"问题（西方的、受过教育的、工业化的、富裕的、民主的）。如果期刊编辑主要是来自美国的男性，那么他们可能会更重视与西方男性人口相关的研究论文，无论是有意识还是无意识地。

items.text:
Could you get by without using the internet for four and a half years? That's exactly what singer and actress Selena Gomez has done in a bid to improve her mental health.
She has spoken extensively about the relationship between her social media usage and her mental wellbeing, recalling feeling like “an addict” when she became Instagram's most followed user in 2016. “Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health”, says she. “The unnecessary hate and comparisons went away once I put my phone down.”
Ditching the web at large, however, is a far more subtle and complicated prospect. The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection. Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege.
Ms Gomez's multi-millionaire status has allowed her to take the “social” out of social media, so she can continue to leverage her enormous fame while keeping the _trolls_ (恶意挑衅的帖子) at bay. The fact that she's still the second most-followed woman on Instagram suggests it's entirely possible to maintain a significant web profile to promote various projects - by way of a dedicated team - without being exposed to the cruel comments, hate mail, and rape or death threats.
It goes without saying that this is fundamentally different from how the rest of us without beauty deals and films to publicise use the likes of Instagram, TikTok, and Twitter, but even the concept of a digital _detox_ (戒瘾) requires having a device and connectivity to choose to disconnect from.
The UK's digital divide has worsened over the past two years, leaving poorer families without broadband connections in their homes. Digital exclusion is a major threat to wider societal equality in the UK, so witnessing companies like Facebook championing the _metaverse_ (元宇宙) as the next great frontier when schoolchildren are struggling to complete their homework feels particularly irritating.
Consequently, it's worth bearing in mind that while deleting all social media accounts will undoubtedly make some feel infinitely better, many other people benefit from the strong sense of community that sharing platforms can breed.
Internet access will continue to grow in importance as we edge further towards web 3.0, and greater resources and initiatives are needed to provide the underprivileged with the connectivity they desperately need to learn, work, and live. It's crucial that people who feel that social media is having a detrimental effect on their mental health are allowed to switch off and for those living in digital exclusion to be able to switch on in the first place.

q5.stem: What do we learn about singer and actress Selena Gomez in the past four and a half years?
options: She has had worsening mental problems.
She has won Instagram's most followers.
She has refrained from using social media.
She has succeeded in a bid on the internet
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Could you get by without using the internet for four and a half years? That's exactly what singer and actress Selena Gomez has done in a bid to improve her mental health.」
排除：A：文中称其改善心理健康，未说问题恶化；B：2016年曾最多，文中现称其第二；D：in a bid to意为尝试，非网络竞标成功。
q5.stemCn: 关于歌手兼演员赛琳娜·戈麦斯，我们在过去四年半里了解到什么？
optionsCn: 她经历了恶化的心理问题。
她赢得了Instagram最多的粉丝。
她一直避免使用社交媒体。
她成功完成了一次互联网上的尝试。

q5.stem: Why does actively opting out of using the internet become a matter of privilege?
options: Most people find it subtle and complicated to give up using the internet.
Most people can hardly ditch the web while avoiding hate and comparisons.
Most people can hardly get by without the internet due to growing digitisation.
Most people have been seriously addicted to the web without being aware of it.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection. Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege.」
排除：A：仅说戒网复杂，未解释特权原因，答非所问；B：恶帖随放下手机消失，并非难戒网原因，混淆因果；D：仅她自述上瘾，非多数人未察觉，以偏概全。
q5.stemCn: 为什么主动选择不使用互联网会成为一种特权？
optionsCn: 大多数人认为戒掉互联网是微妙而复杂的。
大多数人很难在避免仇恨和比较的同时戒掉网络。
由于日益增长的数字化，大多数人很难在没有互联网的情况下生活。
大多数人已经严重沉迷于网络，却没有意识到这一点。

q5.stem: Why does the author say “witnessing companies...feels particularly irritating” (Lines 2-4, Para. 6)?
options: The UK digital divide would further worsen due to the metaverse.
The concept of the metaverse is believed to be still quite illusory.
School children would be drawn farther away from the real world.
Most families in the UK do not have stable broadband connections.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「The UK's digital divide has worsened over the past two years, leaving poorer families without broadband connections in their homes. Digital exclusion is a major threat to wider societal equality in the UK, so witnessing companies like Facebook championing the _metaverse_ (元宇宙) as the next great frontier when schoolchildren are struggling to complete their homework feels particularly irritating.」
排除：B：原文未说元宇宙虚幻，而是强调数字鸿沟，非此项理由。；C：原文未说孩子远离现实，而是说缺网致不公平，错解原因。；D：原文指贫困家庭缺宽带，非多数英国家庭，范围扩大。
q5.stemCn: 作者为什么说“目睹公司……尤其令人恼火”（第6段第2-4行）？
optionsCn: 由于元宇宙，英国的数字鸿沟将进一步恶化。
人们认为，元宇宙的概念仍然相当虚幻。
学童将会被进一步拉离现实世界。
英国的大多数家庭没有稳定的宽带连接。

q5.stem: What is worth bearing in mind concerning social media platforms?
options: They are conducive to promoting societal equality.
They help many people feel connected with others.
They provide a necessary device for a digital detox.
They create a virtual community on the internet.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Consequently, it's worth bearing in mind that while deleting all social media accounts will undoubtedly make some feel infinitely better, many other people benefit from the strong sense of community that sharing platforms can breed.」
排除：A：与原文相反，数字排斥威胁平等；C：无中生有，戒断需设备非平台提供；D：偷换概念，社区感非虚拟社区。
q5.stemCn: 关于社交媒体平台，有什么值得记住的吗？
optionsCn: 它们有助于促进社会平等。
它们帮助许多人感觉与他人有联系。
它们为数字排毒提供了一个必要的工具。
它们在互联网上创建了一个虚拟社区。

q5.stem: What does the author think is really important for those living in digital exclusion?
options: Having access to the internet.
Edging further towards web 3.0.
Getting more educational resources.
Opening more social media accounts.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「It's crucial that people who feel that social media is having a detrimental effect on their mental health are allowed to switch off and for those living in digital exclusion to be able to switch on in the first place.」
排除：B：web3.0只是发展趋势的背景，不是重点；C：教育资源只覆盖学习，原文核心是整体接入；D：与原文相反，问题在于缺少接入而非账号。
q5.stemCn: 作者认为，对于生活在数字鸿沟中的人们来说，什么才是真正重要的？
optionsCn: 能够接入互联网。
进一步迈向Web 3.0。
获取更多的教育资源。
开设更多的社交媒体账户。

items.cn:
你能四年半不使用互联网吗？这正是歌手兼演员赛琳娜·戈麦斯为了改善心理健康所做的尝试。
她曾广泛谈论社交媒体使用与心理健康之间的关系，回忆起2016年成为Instagram上关注人数最多的用户时，感觉自己像个"瘾君子"。她说："远离社交媒体是我为心理健康做出的最好决定。一旦我放下手机，那些不必要的仇恨和比较就消失了。"
然而，完全放弃网络是一个更加微妙和复杂的问题。我们社会日益数字化意味着，从支付燃气账单到规划去朋友家的路线，甚至打电话，一切都依赖于你的网络连接。主动选择不使用互联网成为一种特权。
戈麦斯女士的百万富翁身份让她能够将社交媒体中的"社交"因素剥离，这样她可以继续利用其巨大的知名度，同时远离恶意挑衅的帖子。她仍然是Instagram上关注人数第二多的女性这一事实表明，完全有可能通过专门的团队维持一个重要的网络形象来推广各种项目，而无需暴露在残酷的评论、仇恨邮件、强奸或死亡威胁之下。
不言而喻，这与我们这些没有美容合约和电影需要宣传的人使用Instagram、TikTok和Twitter的方式有着根本的不同，但即使是数字戒瘾的概念也需要拥有设备和连接才能选择断开连接。
过去两年，英国的数字鸿沟扩大了，导致较贫困家庭家中没有宽带连接。数字排斥是英国更广泛社会平等的主要威胁，因此，当学生们努力完成家庭作业时，目睹像Facebook这样的公司将元宇宙作为下一个伟大前沿来推广，感觉特别令人恼火。
因此，值得记住的是，虽然删除所有社交媒体账户无疑会让一些人感觉好得多，但许多人受益于共享平台可以培养的强烈社区感。
随着我们逐渐迈向Web 3.0，互联网接入的重要性将继续增长，需要更多的资源和举措来为弱势群体提供他们迫切需要的连接，以便学习、工作和生活。至关重要的是，那些认为社交媒体对其心理健康产生负面影响的人应该被允许关闭社交媒体，而那些生活在数字排斥中的人首先应该能够接入网络。

items.text:
Psychologists have long been in disagreement as to whether competition is a learned or a genetic component of human behavior. Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life.
Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives. According to Sigmund Freud, humans are born screaming for attention and full of organic drives for fulfillment in various areas. Initially, we compete for the attention of our parents. Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.
Current work in _anthropology_ (人类学) has suggested, however, that this view of the role of competition in human behavior may be incorrect. Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the “natural world,” that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being “nasty, brutish, and short.” This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work, _The Origin of Species_, which established the doctrine of natural selection. This doctrine, which takes for granted that those species best able to adapt to and master the natural environment in which they live will survive, has suggested that the struggle for survival is an inherent human trait which determines a person's success. Darwin's theory has even been summarized as “survival of the fittest” — a phrase Darwin himself never used — further highlighting competition's role in success.
As it has often been pointed out, however, there is nothing in the concept of natural selection that suggests that competition is the most successful strategy for survival of the fittest. Darwin asserted in _The Origin of Species_ that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation.
Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition as opposed to other values, such as cooperation — by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable. In 1937, the world-renowned anthropologist Margaret Mead published _Cooperation and Competition among Primitive Peoples_, based on her studies of several societies that did not prize competition, and, in fact, seemed at times to place a negative value on it. One such society was the Zuni Indians of Arizona, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition. After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it.

q5.stem: What does the author think is easy to see in many areas of contemporary life?
options: The disagreement on the inevitability of competition.
The consequence of psychological investigation.
The effect of human drives.
The impact of competition.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life.」
排除：A：无中生有，作者说的是能认识到竞争的作用，非竞争不可避免的分歧；B：张冠李戴，原文称竞争是人的本能后果，非心理调查的后果；C：偷换概念，易见的是竞争发挥的作用，不是人类本能驱动的作用。
q5.stemCn: 作者认为在当代生活的许多领域中，什么是显而易见的？
optionsCn: 对竞争不可避免性的分歧。
心理调查的后果。
人类动力的影响。
竞争的影响。

q5.stem: According to psychology, what do people strive to do following the initial stage of their life?
options: Fulfill individual needs without incurring adverse effects of human drives.
Indulge in cultural pursuits while keeping their base impulses at bay.
Gain extensive recognition without exposing pure indulgence.
Satisfy their own desires while observing social conventions.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.」
排除：A：原文未提避免人类驱力负面影响，属无中生有；B：将文化规范偷换为文化放纵，与原文相反；C：追求广泛认可属过度引申，原文仅指父母注意。
q5.stemCn: 根据心理学，人们在生命的初始阶段之后努力做什么？
optionsCn: 满足个人需求，同时避免人类驱动力带来的不良影响。
投身于文化活动，同时抑制他们的基本冲动。
获得广泛的认可，同时不暴露纯粹的放纵。
满足他们自己的欲望，同时遵守社会规范。

q5.stem: What do we learn about the “natural world” characterized by Thomas Hobbes?
options: It gets misrepresented by philosophers and anthropologists.
It gets distorted in Darwin's _The Origin of Species_.
It is free from the rational intervention of humans.
It is the pre-rational world rarely appreciated nowadays.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the “natural world,” that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being “nasty, brutish, and short.”」
排除：A项未说自然世界被误传；B项未说达尔文歪曲该书；D项未说如今少有人欣赏
q5.stemCn: 托马斯·霍布斯所描述的“自然世界”是怎样的？
optionsCn: 它被哲学家和人类学家所曲解。
它在达尔文的《物种起源》中被歪曲。
它不受人类理性的干预。
它是如今很少被欣赏的前理性的世界。

q5.stem: What can we conclude from Darwin's assertion in _The Origin of Species_?
options: All species inherently depend on others for survival.
Struggles for survival do not exclude mutual support.
Competition weighs as much as cooperation as a survival strategy.
The strongest species proves to be the fittest in natural selection.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Darwin asserted in _The Origin of Species_ that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation.」
排除：A：原文未说所有物种必然依赖他者，属夸大；C：原文未比较竞争与合作权重，属偷换；D：达尔文强调挣扎为隐喻，非最强竞争，相反
q5.stemCn: 我们可以从《物种起源》中达尔文的论断得出什么结论？
optionsCn: 所有物种都天生依赖其他物种才能生存。
生存斗争并不排除相互支持。
作为一种生存策略，竞争与合作同等重要。
在自然选择中，最强壮的物种被证明是最适者。

q5.stem: What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach after studying dozens of different cultures?
options: It is characteristic of humans to be competitive.
Americans are uniquely opposed to cooperation.
Competition is relatively more prevalent in Western societies.
People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it.」
排除：A：将“文化塑造的竞争”偷换为人类天生特质，与原文相反；B：原文仅说美国人推崇竞争，无“反对合作”依据；C：范围过窄且无据，未提及西方社会竞争更普遍
q5.stemCn: 玛格丽特·米德在研究了数十种不同的文化之后得出了什么结论？
optionsCn: 人类的特征是好竞争。
美国人独特地反对合作。
竞争在西方社会中相对更普遍。
人们对竞争的态度实际上是受文化制约的。

items.cn:
心理学家们长期以来一直就竞争是人类行为的习得性组成部分还是遗传性组成部分存在分歧。无论它是什么，你都无法不承认竞争在学术和当代生活的许多其他领域所产生的影响。
从心理学的角度来看，竞争被视为人类驱动的必然结果。根据西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的理论，人类天生就渴望关注，并在各个领域充满满足自我的有机驱动力。起初，我们竞争以获得父母的关注。此后，我们便听任于自我满足的本能冲动与禁止纯粹放纵的社会和文化规范之间的斗争摆布。
然而，当前的人类学研究（人类学）表明，这种关于竞争在人类行为中作用的观点可能是错误的。十七世纪伟大的哲学家之一托马斯·霍布斯，或许最让人记住的是他对"自然世界"的描述，即人类意志施加之前的世界，是"丑陋、野蛮且短暂的"。这种前理性世界的形象仍然被广泛接受，并查尔斯·达尔文极具影响力的著作《物种起源》所强化，该书确立了自然选择的学说。这一学说理所当然地认为，最能适应并掌握其生存环境的物种将会生存下来，这表明生存斗争是一种决定人类成功的内在特质。达尔文的理论甚至被概括为"适者生存"——一个达尔文本人从未使用过的短语——进一步强调了竞争在成功中的作用。
然而，正如人们经常指出的那样，自然选择的概念中没有任何内容表明竞争是最适者生存的最成功策略。达尔文在《物种起源》中断言，他所描述的斗争应被视为隐喻，并且可以轻易地包含依赖与合作。
许多研究已经进行，以测试不同文化对竞争相对于其他价值（如合作）的重视程度，并且普遍得出的结论是，美国人独特地将竞争视为自然的、不可避免的和值得称赞的。1937年，世界著名的人类学家玛格丽特·米德出版了《原始民族中的合作与竞争》，该书基于她对几个不重视竞争的社会的研究，事实上，这些社会有时似乎对竞争持负面评价。其中一个是亚利桑那州的祖尼印第安人，米德发现，他们高度重视合作远胜于竞争。在研究了数十种此类文化后，米德的最终结论是，竞争性是人类行为中一个文化创造的方面，它在特定社会中的普遍程度与该社会对其重视的程度相关。

items.text:
Research is meant to benefit society by raising public awareness and creating products and innovations that enhance development. For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.
Findings effectively communicated can go a long way to serve the interests of the public. They can help address social injustices or improve treatments offered to patients.
Many researchers seem to be content with sharing the results of their studies in academic journals or at conferences. But few journals allow everybody to read the findings. Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.
For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritized.
Many researchers lack the writing skills to describe their results to a general audience. They may also worry about whether the public will understand their findings, or about findings being used to influence controversial policies. These concerns cause some researchers to shy away from communicating their findings outside the academic community.
Propagating research findings beyond academic publications is particularly crucial for addressing certain social discrepancies. It can help families, communities, healthcare providers, policymakers, government agencies and others to understand and respond to crises that plague society.
The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways. Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.
To benefit both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated.
Institutions and funding organizations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn't have to pay to read them. Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.
Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public. Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent.
There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public.
Sharing results with the people who are most affected by them makes us better researchers and ensures that our work can be used to improve people's lives. Institutions and collaborators must recognize the value of doing so.

q5.stem: How can research serve its full purpose according to the author?
options: With researchers being aware of public interests.
With its findings published in prominent journals.
With researchers creating products that enhance social development.
With its findings properly communicated beyond the academic circle.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.」
排除：A：无中生有，研究者意识到公共利益非关键；B：偷换概念，顶刊发表并非完整目的；C：范围过窄，产品创新未涵盖成果传播。
q5.stemCn: 根据作者的观点，研究如何才能充分发挥其作用？
optionsCn: 研究人员意识到公众利益。
其研究成果发表在著名期刊上。
研究人员创造促进社会发展的产品。
其研究成果在学术界之外得到有效传播。

q5.stem: Why do ordinary readers find it difficult to access the results of researchers' studies?
options: They cannot understand the academic language used for reporting these results.
They feel intimidated by the jargon researchers use to describe their findings.
They do not attend conferences where these results are freely available.
They have few chances to locate the journals that publish these findings.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.」
排除：B：原文只说语言难懂，未提因行话而畏惧，属无中生有；C：原文未说会议成果自由可得，属无中生有；D：读不到不等于找不到期刊，属偷换概念。
q5.stemCn: 为什么普通读者觉得难以获取研究人员的研究结果？
optionsCn: 他们无法理解用于报告这些结果的学术语言。
他们畏惧研究人员用来描述其发现的行话。
他们不参加这些结果可自由获取的会议。
他们很少有找到发表这些研究成果的期刊的机会。

q5.stem: What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritize communicating their findings to the public?
options: They can thrive on the papers published.
Their top consideration is to win tenure.
Their main goal is gaining recognition in their field.
They have to struggle to reach out to the community.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritized.」
排除：A：原文仅说论文有助于终身教职，未说靠论文兴旺；C：原文主目标是争取终身教职，非领域认可；D：原文未指出社区外联艰苦，属无中生有
q5.stemCn: 一些研究人员不优先考虑向公众传达其研究成果的原因之一是什么？
optionsCn: 他们可以依靠已发表的论文来取得成功。
他们首要的考虑是获得终身教职。
他们主要的目标是在自己的领域获得认可。
他们必须努力与社区建立联系。

q5.stem: How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves?
options: By helping them to identify new research directions.
By enabling them to understand crises plaguing society.
By enabling them to effectively address social discrepancies.
By helping them to forge ties with government agencies.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.」
排除：B：受益者是公众等而非研究者，非自身收益；C：属社会收益，非研究者自身收益；D：新联系未指政府机构，偷换概念
q5.stemCn: 分享研究成果如何能对研究人员自身有益？
optionsCn: 通过帮助他们确定新的研究方向。
通过使他们能够理解困扰社会的危机。
通过使他们能够有效解决社会差异。
通过帮助他们与政府机构建立联系。

q5.stem: Why are researchers advised to engage the services of professional writers or communication officers?
options: To satisfy ethics committees' mandatory requirements of researchers.
To translate their study into languages accessible to readers overseas.
To make their publications correctly understood by the public.
To render their findings acceptable by prominent journals.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public.」
排除：A：强制分享非请写手原因，无中生有；B：通俗语言非海外语言，偷换概念；D：面向期刊发表非原因，张冠李戴。
q5.stemCn: 为什么研究人员被建议聘请专业作家或传播官员？
optionsCn: 为了满足伦理委员会对研究人员的强制性要求。
将他们的研究翻译成海外读者能理解的语言。
使他们的出版物被公众正确理解。
使他们的研究成果被著名期刊接受。

items.cn:
研究旨在通过提高公众意识、创造促进发展的产品和创新来造福社会。为了使研究充分发挥其作用，研究成果必须走出研究实验室和学术期刊的局限。
有效地传播研究发现可以极大地服务于公众利益。它们可以帮助解决社会不公，或改善提供给患者的治疗方案。
许多研究人员似乎满足于在学术期刊或会议上分享他们的研究成果。但很少有期刊允许所有人阅读这些发现。即使是免费获取的文章，通常也使用普通读者难以理解的学术语言写成。
对于处于终身教职轨道上的研究人员来说，他们的主要目标是获得终身教职，这在一定程度上可以通过在知名期刊上发表多篇论文来实现。此类压力意味着社区层面的外联工作并未得到优先考虑。
许多研究人员缺乏向普通受众描述其研究成果的写作技巧。他们也可能担心公众是否能理解他们的发现，或者担心这些发现会被用来影响有争议的政策。这些顾虑导致一些研究人员回避在学术界之外传播他们的研究成果。
在学术出版物之外传播研究发现对于解决某些社会差异尤为重要。它可以帮助家庭、社区、医疗服务提供者、政策制定者、政府机构及其他各方理解和应对困扰社会的危机。
分享研究成果的好处是双向的。与其他研究人员和公众进行互动可以带来意想不到的新联系和新想法，这些新想法可能为研究指明富有成果的新方向。
为了让研究人员和社区双方都受益，寻找创新且易于分享研究成果的方式，其重要性怎么强调都不为过。
机构和资助组织应支持更多研究人员在开放获取期刊上发表文章，这样公众就不必付费阅读。机构和研究人员应投资于能够更广泛地扩展成果分享能力的合作伙伴关系。
此外，伦理委员会应强制研究人员向公众分享他们的研究成果。每位研究参与者都应选择是否接收研究结果，这是知情同意过程的一部分。
由于专业术语的存在，公众可能会误解研究人员提出的研究发现。但研究人员可以聘请专业作家或传播官员来帮助他们将研究转化为更易于理解的语言，并与媒体和公众广泛分享，从而解决这个问题。
与受研究成果影响最大的人分享成果，能让我们成为更好的研究者，并确保我们的工作能够被用来改善人们的生活。机构和合作者必须认识到这样做的价值。

items.text:
Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn. This is the mating season of some of the most common varieties, when male house spiders come out of hidden corners to look for females, and garden spiders reach adult size and spin their most dazzling webs.
Yet while the spider is a familiar fixture of nursery poems or songs and Halloween decorations, its relationship with humans is complicated. Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers. Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk. Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless. Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops. But they are a constant source of human anxieties — with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.
Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis? British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them. But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out. And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders.
The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.
Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland. Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas. With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors.
It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds, or butterflies, in spite of their unique status as nature's spinners. But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.

蜘蛛在八月底到整个初秋时节都能感受到它们的存在。这是某些最常见蜘蛛品种的交配季节，此时雄性家蜘蛛会从隐蔽的角落出来寻找雌性，而园蜘蛛则长成成年体型，编织出它们最令人惊叹的网。
然而，尽管蜘蛛是儿歌、歌曲和万圣节装饰中常见的元素，它与人类的关系却很复杂。对蜘蛛的恐惧很普遍，并对患者的生活产生严重影响。这种恐惧的普遍性似乎与任何理性的风险评估都无关。英国的蜘蛛几乎都是无害的。农田蜘蛛品种通过捕食与我们争夺作物的昆虫，提供了宝贵的生态系统服务。但它们是人类焦虑的持续来源——与女巫和邪恶的文化联系可以追溯到中世纪。
这是否在一定程度上解释了在我们这个生态危机时代，关于蜘蛛状况的数据缺乏的原因？由于长期以来有收集和观察蝴蝶的传统，英国蝴蝶是世界上研究最多的昆虫群体。但蜘蛛保护主义者指出，直到20世纪80年代，家蜘蛛的分类才得到妥善整理。虽然关于昆虫种群的信息是通过测量撞击挡风玻璃或捕捉装置数量的实验收集的，但很少有人尝试统计蜘蛛的数量。
飞行昆虫数量的巨大减少只能意味着蜘蛛食物供应的减少。最近的一项标志性研究确定了1989年至2016年间昆虫种群下降了75%，农药使用被认为是罪魁祸首之一，同时为开发而破坏野生区域也是原因。这意味着蜘蛛的整体状况令人担忧，就像大多数生物一样。但保护主义者最担心的是那些因栖息地丧失和碎片化而受到威胁的品种，这使得它们无法迁徙。
在英国定期记录的约650种蜘蛛中，大多数在沼泽和荒地中茁壮成长。保护工作通常由坚定的个人领导，通过将它们重新引入新区域，帮助一些物种恢复。随着重新野化现在牢固地列入环境政策议程，希望未来蜘蛛能够自行迁徙，沿着野生动物走廊移动以适应气候变化。
尽管蜘蛛作为自然的编织者有着独特的地位，但它们似乎永远无法像蜜蜂、鸟类或蝴蝶那样吸引同等程度的人类热情。但当它们在这个秋天以全部的辉煌展现自己时，如果更多的动物爱好者认识到蜘蛛的非凡之处，那将是一件好事。
